threatModel.summary: Jubarte is a local Rust Word-document toolkit exposed through Rust byte APIs, PyO3 Python, WASM/Node, native and language CLIs, and an optional Python MCP server over stdio. Untrusted DOCX/DOC/Markdown and JSON edit plans feed package admission, XML/legacy parsers, comparisons, edits and PDF/PNG rendering. Native publication and explicit self-update are separate host-authority boundaries (src/lib.rs:7-30,106-174; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798; jubarte-python/python/jubarte_redlines/mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381). An independent architecture reviewer identified the resource rows below before its execution was interrupted; parent verified their actual consumers offline.
assets: Host process availability and bounded memory/CPU while parsing attacker-authored documents (src/admission.rs:42-105; src/legacy_doc.rs:179-216).
Integrity/confidentiality of source documents and generated output; edit snapshot SHA-256 and output alias guards (src/bin/jubarte.rs:1610-1667,1768-1826).
Files outside MCP's held root capability and the operator's installed executable (src/publication.rs:146-200; src/update.rs:198-257,299-321).
Release/registry authority and signing credentials supplied by the operator or CI secret store, never document contents (.github/workflows/release.yml:261-310; scripts/release.sh:976-1012).
trustBoundaries: Document author -> Rust parsing/rendering -> caller process. admission bounds compressed bytes, entry counts, per-part/total inflation and selected XML depth/tag policy; downstream XML, numeric layout, images/fonts and legacy fields require their own effective controls (src/admission.rs:442-580,788-827; src/convert/mod.rs:769-798).

Python/Node/native CLI callers choose ambient local input/output paths; these callers already possess operator file authority. MCP clients instead provide relative document/output names beneath --root, default current working directory; build_server resolves that root once and _OutputRoot retains native cap_std::Dir authority for actual I/O (mcp_server.py:67-112,373-381; jubarte-python/src/lib.rs:1244-1279; src/publication.rs:146-200).

MCP/native rendering -> ambient font resources: JUBARTE_FONT_DIR overrides the platform user font directory; macOS ~/Library/Application Support/jubarte/fonts, Unix $XDG_DATA_HOME/jubarte/fonts or ~/.local/share/jubarte/fonts, Windows %APPDATA%/jubarte/fonts. Fonts are read by conversion outside the document root (src/convert/font.rs:2637-2652).

Rendering -> persistent font index: JUBARTE_FONT_INDEX selects a path; empty/off disables it; default parent(user_font_dir)/font-index.tsv. FONT_INDEX loads that path and save merges and writes path.with_extension(tsv.<pid>.tmp), then renames it to the index (src/convert/font.rs:3100-3107,3213-3229). This is component ambient authority, distinct from tool document/output confinement.

Explicit self-update -> fixed jandira-tech/jubarte-redlines GitHub release and SHA256SUMS.txt -> extracted platform executable -> installed binary. TLS/checksum verification, optional compiled version-gated signing policy, and lstat regular-file hook enforce distinct steps (src/update.rs:25-48,198-257,274-285,299-321; Cargo.toml:137-148).

Privileged release workflows: release.yml optionally signs with secret-store ZIPSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY, computes SHA256SUMS.txt and publishes GitHub assets. Operator scripts/release.sh:976-1012 can recover workflow artifacts into dist/release, compute checksums and create a release without that signing step.
attackerCapabilities: An attacker can author DOCX ZIP entries, relationship targets/types, XML structures and numeric attributes, embedded media/font bytes, legacy DOC character streams, Markdown and edit-plan values that a caller elects to process.

An MCP client can invoke registered tools over its existing stdio connection and request reads/writes within the granted root; overwrite=true explicitly permits replacement there. No remote listener or tenant model is established by the source (mcp_server.py:93-112,373-381).

Document control does not imply control of host environment variables, font directories/index, release assets, signing credentials, operator checkout or trusted MCP root. No new authority is inferred from already possessing those privileges.
securityObjectives: Reject malformed or excessive document input before unbounded recursion, scalar-driven allocation or algorithmic amplification reaches the host process.
Keep document relationship resolution within in-memory package data and do not fetch external references (src/convert/mod.rs:21310-21319; src/admission.rs:14-23).
Enforce held-root filesystem confinement and no-clobber publication; retain source identity for guarded native edits (src/publication.rs:419-574; src/bin/jubarte.rs:1610-1667,1768-1826).
Install only checksum-verified release binaries and enforce configured signing keys/version rules and regular-file validation; never expose CI secret material in generated analysis.
assumptions: Exact userContext is null; no supplied threat model or CODEX_SECURITY_KNOWLEDGE_BASE was present. Only current on-disk source was reviewed; no Git history, network, application execution or credential validation was used.

Rust library, Python and WASM hosts may pass adversarial documents; no specific internet-facing production deployment is assumed. SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits; caller-enforced isolation constrains blast radius but does not establish parser safety.

MCP docstring claims tools only touch files under root (mcp_server.py:67-68), while native font resolution/index uses ambient directories (font.rs:2637-2652,3100-3107,3213-3229). Retain that guarantee mismatch; no attacker-directed file disclosure or arbitrary overwrite beyond trusted font configuration was established.

Compiled RELEASE_KEYS is empty and FIRST_SIGNED_RELEASE is None (src/update.rs:44-48), so current verification is checksum-only. docs/SELF_UPDATE.md:59-87 acknowledges this. The operator fallback release path lacks signing, a future signing-era compatibility concern rather than an established present substitution vulnerability.

Runtime and deployment-specific exploit reliability remain untested. The interrupted architecture/baseline workers did not return final fully-reviewed inventories; partial review and remaining paths must remain explicit.

findings.title: Rendering a small DOCX table can exhaust host memory
findings.summary: A document author can set `w:gridSpan`, `w:gridBefore`, or `w:gridAfter` to a large integer. PDF/PNG layout uses it directly as a vector length, so a tiny admitted document can demand gigabytes and terminate or stall the host process.

severity.rationale: An untrusted document can deterministically drive huge allocations through a public parser boundary. This compromises availability of the rendering process; shared-service exposure is conditional and process memory limits constrain the blast radius.

confidence.rationale: Static source tracing establishes the unbounded usize parsing and direct vector allocation after admission, with no semantic span budget. No application code was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled memory allocation from table spans

codeEvidence.label: render entry
codeEvidence.explanation: Rendering admits package bytes, then opens the normalized package.

codeEvidence.label: table dispatch
codeEvidence.explanation: Body tables reach table_block with document-controlled XML.

codeEvidence.label: table span
codeEvidence.explanation: gridSpan is parsed as usize and only a minimum of one is enforced.

codeEvidence.label: table skips
codeEvidence.explanation: gridBefore and gridAfter use the same unbounded span representation.

codeEvidence.label: table allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Summed attacker-controlled occupancy directly sizes the grid vector.

codeEvidence.label: table merges
codeEvidence.explanation: The same unbounded span sizes the merge bookkeeping vector.

rootCause.summary: `table_block()` obtains cell and omitted-column spans from XML. `cell_span()` and `row_grid_skip()` only enforce positive values. It sums these values into occupancy and grows grid and merge vectors to that length, independently of the document byte and nesting limits.

findings.remediation: Bound each span and total table occupancy before allocation using a documented renderer limit; use checked arithmetic and refuse excessive grids consistently across gridSpan, gridBefore and gridAfter.

counterEvidence: ZIP, inflated bytes and XML nesting are bounded before layout.
The security policy recommends process CPU/memory limits; these limit damage to a worker but do not reject the document.
limitations: No runtime denial-of-service input was executed.
validation.summary: The public renderer calls admission and then walks body tables. A one-cell table with a span of 1073741824 remains shallow, small XML yet requests a 4 GiB f32 grid before additional bookkeeping. The byte/depth admission checks do not constrain numeric table widths.

dataflow.summary: DOCX bytes -> with_layout -> admitted XML DOM -> body table_block -> cell_span/row_grid_skip -> occupancy -> Vec resize and merge allocation.

impact.rationale: Memory exhaustion or process termination; no code execution or data access is established.

likelihood.rationale: Direct integer-to-allocation path reachable with a tiny document.

reachability.summary: A document author needs only to have their package passed to the public rendering API; no filesystem access or privileged configuration is required.

attackPath.summary: Supply a small DOCX with a visible body table and an enormous grid span, then ask a Rust, Python, WASM or CLI consumer to render it.

remediationTests: Check that a tiny table with an enormous gridSpan is refused before allocation.
Cover gridBefore/gridAfter, accumulated spans, and overflow boundaries.

originalCandidates.title: Rendering a small table with attacker-selected gridSpan can allocate enormous column vectors
originalCandidates.hypothesis: A tiny admitted main document can set gridSpan to a huge usize; allocation amplification is independent of ZIP/XML input-byte/depth limits.

findings.title: Rendering an auxiliary part with a non-XML extension bypasses XML depth limits
findings.summary: A document author can point a theme or other parsed auxiliary relationship at a deeply nested XML part named `.bin`. Admission applies its XML limits by filename, but rendering loads these parts by relationship type and recursively parses them, allowing a small package to exhaust the host stack.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document bytes cross a public parser boundary and can terminate the rendering process. External shared-service exposure is conditional; no code execution or file access is established.

confidence.rationale: Parent independently verified the extension-based admission gate, relationship-selected consumer and unchecked recursive parser. Runtime stack threshold was not tested.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled recursion through an admission bypass

codeEvidence.label: extension gate
codeEvidence.explanation: Only names ending .xml or .rels are passed through the XML depth/tag-policy gate; other bytes are merely drained.

codeEvidence.label: main only extra
codeEvidence.explanation: The extension exception validates only the main part, leaving auxiliary relationship targets unchecked.

codeEvidence.label: render open
codeEvidence.explanation: Public render pipeline admits then opens the normalized package.

codeEvidence.label: theme target
codeEvidence.explanation: A relationship type chooses an internal part without an extension constraint.

codeEvidence.label: theme dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Theme bytes are passed to the unchecked recursive DOM parser.

codeEvidence.label: styles dom
codeEvidence.explanation: The same by-type loader also reaches the styles parser.

codeEvidence.label: numbering dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Numbering relationships also select arbitrary-named XML.

codeEvidence.label: comments dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Comment relationships feed unchecked XML parsing.

codeEvidence.label: note targets
codeEvidence.explanation: Comments and notes are selected from package relationship targets.

codeEvidence.label: endnotes dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Endnote XML reaches the recursive DOM parser.

codeEvidence.label: footnotes dom
codeEvidence.explanation: Footnote XML reaches the recursive DOM parser.

codeEvidence.label: xml recursion
codeEvidence.explanation: A nested start tag recursively enters parse_element without a depth counter.

rootCause.summary: Admission validates XML depth and tags for `.xml`/`.rels` and specially the main document. Rendering independently resolves auxiliary parts by relationship type; theme, styles, numbering, comments and notes can therefore carry XML under another extension and enter `parse_element()` without the promised gate.

findings.remediation: Apply the active XML limits to every part at its XML consumer or identify all XML parts by content type/relationship use before parsing; also make DOM construction iterative or enforce a depth bound there.

counterEvidence: Nonstandard main-part names receive an extra depth check.
Package size, inflation, CRC, paths and ZIP consistency are checked.
External relationships are unnecessary; this uses an internal package target.
limitations: No runtime exploit or deployment was tested; exact nesting required to exhaust a stack depends on host/build.
validation.summary: A valid small package can keep main/metadata parts conventionally named while assigning a `/theme` relationship to `word/theme/theme1.bin`. Byte budgets still apply, but the auxiliary payload bypasses `check_xml_depth()` and is parsed recursively by `load_theme()`. Confirmed sibling consumers include styles, numbering, comments, endnotes and footnotes.

dataflow.summary: DOCX auxiliary .bin -> admission drains only -> by-type relationship resolution -> part_string -> load_theme/other auxiliary parser -> parse_element recursion.

impact.rationale: Stack exhaustion and availability loss of the caller process.

likelihood.rationale: No privileged setting is required; only attacker-authored document processing.

reachability.summary: An untrusted DOCX author controls both relationship target and part contents. Public Rust render APIs are sufficient; language bindings forwarding them inherit the issue.

attackPath.summary: Provide a DOCX with a deeply nested auxiliary XML payload under a non-XML extension, reference it as the theme, then request PDF/PNG rendering.

remediationTests: Reject an over-depth `.bin` theme with a typed XML refusal.
Cover styles, numbering, comments, footnotes and endnotes with nonstandard part extensions.

surfaces.label: Document admission and downstream XML parser consistency
surfaces.notes: Validated xml-depth-nonxml-part: extension-based admission misses auxiliary XML resolved by relationship type (admission.rs:533,556; convert/mod.rs:3305-3317,21310-21319; xmllinq/parse.rs:661).

originalCandidate.originalEvidence: admission.rs only check_xml_depth on .xml/.rels plus main part, but auxiliary relationships can target e.g theme/theme1.bin. convert::main_rel_part follows type /theme regardless extension, load_theme→parse_theme_xml→Dom::parse_xdocument and parse.rs:661 recursively calls parse_element with no depth guard. Small deeply nested .bin theme can pass admission then stack-overflow.

candidate.originalEvidence: src/legacy_doc.rs:1604 (Story::blocks): fields.iter().any(|&code| code) runs before every input character; 0x13 pushes true, 0x14 sets top false, 0x15 pops. A compressed-text story ('\x13\x14').repeat(N) builds N all-false frames; each subsequent begin/separator and displayed text rescans all N frames. No nesting limit in read()/main_text()/blocks, so ~200 KB story with 100k open/separated fields requires ~10^10 bool visits, without exceeding byte-size limits.

candidate.originalEvidence:
Repeat sibling

elements under w:body. quick-xml parses these as Empty with tag p a=/; TagPolicy::tolerant uses html_attributes and permits unquoted value /. Admission sees depth 2. Permissive Parser::parse_element lines 574-593 blindly treats first / after = as opening quote, consumes second / as closing quote, leaving > and treating the empty element as an OPEN element; at line 661 recursively parses each following sibling as child => unbounded recursion despite max_xml_depth256.
